## Triage brief — "Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs"

**Identification (p. 1).** Randall Balestriero (Brown University, AMI Labs) and Yann LeCun (NYU, AMI Labs); correspondence rbalestr@brown.edu; released with "Code" and "Live demo" links. The only venue string on the document is the arXiv sidebar/preprint line: arXiv:2610.39302v1 [cs.AI], 29 Oct 2026 — i.e. a preprint, no conference acceptance is claimed (p. 1, p. 16–19 references only).

**Problem attacked (§1, pp. 2–6).** Huh et al.'s Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) — that separately trained modality models converge to one representation of the world as they scale — is an *observation* only: prior support is an idealized contrastive learner whose kernel tends to pointwise mutual information, a deep-linear SGD proof (Ziyin & Chuang), and an explanation of multilingual alignment (p. 2, §6 p. 14). Hence no guarantee, no prediction of *when* alignment holds, and no recipe except "scale up". The paper asks: *when do models trained separately on different modalities provably learn the same representation?*

**Theory (§2, pp. 3–7; full proofs in App. A, pp. 20–23).** A world is a finite state set z∈Z with p(z)>0, rendered injectively per modality x=g_m(z); a JEPA encoder f minimizes L_m(f)=E_{(z,z′)∼π_m}ℓ(f(g_m z), f(g_m z′)) + Ω(f), with ℓ and Ω rotation-invariant and predictor = identity (p. 3, eq. 1). Core results:
- **Lemma 1**: injective rendering only changes coordinates, L_m(f)=L_π(f∘g_m) (p. 3; proof p. 20).
- **Theorem 1 (Platonic Representation Theorem)**: if M≥2 modalities share the positive-pair distribution π₁=…=π_M and minimizers are unique up to rotation, then f*_m∘g_m = Q_m h* with Q_m∈O(k), so any two modalities agree up to the single rotation Q_m Q_m′^⊤ (p. 3).
- **Proposition 1**: with ℓ=‖a−b‖² and whitened second-order anti-collapse, min L_π = 2Σ_{i≤k}(1−μ_i), and minimizers are exactly QΦ_π, Φ_π(z)=(v₁(z),…,v_k(z))/√p(z), under a spectral gap μ_k>μ_{k+1} — a JEPA learns the top eigenvectors of its positive-pair graph (Laplacian eigenmaps) (p. 3).
- **Theorem 2 (kernel mismatch bound)**: min_Q (E_p‖Φ₁−QΦ₂‖²)^{1/2} ≤ (2√2/δ)·min(√k‖K_{π₁}−K_{π₂}‖₂, ‖·‖_F), with δ the eigengap (p. 4, eq. 3); validated on 300 random worlds, error ≤18% of the bound (p. 4, Fig. 2).
- **Proposition 2**: no first/second-moment statistic of unpaired data identifies the rotation (every rotation of a whitened embedding is whitened), but k pairs in general position uniquely determine it by orthogonal Procrustes (p. 4).
- **Theorem 3 (nuisance costs alignment)**: min_Q E‖Qf₁−f₂‖² ≥ 2k(1−min_m ρ(f_m)), where ρ(f)=tr C_f^{1/2}/k is the scene-explained fraction; ρ=1 iff the embedding is a function of the state alone (p. 5, eq. 4).
- **Proposition 3**: good views give ρ=1 (nuisance ignored, Theorem 1 survives with many observations per state); a bad-view JEPA spends r≥1 directions on nuisance — and error ≥2r — iff the corruption keeps more nuisance (β₁) than the world's k-th direction (α_k) (p. 5, formal statement and proof pp. 21–22).
- **Theorem 4**: views + data set the induced world kernel π_{W_m}; spectral solutions are within τ_m of a rotation of Φ(π_{W_m}), and cross-modal misalignment satisfies min_Q RMS − d ≤ τ₁+τ₂ (p. 5, eq. 5; proof pp. 22–23). Synthetic world maps the trade-off: weak views need reach Δ ∝ log N/N samples per state, strong corruptions blur classes, good views align from one sample per state (p. 6, Fig. 4).
- **Proposition 4**: next-token prediction *is* a JEPA — −log softmax = prediction term −⟨h(c),w_y⟩ plus anti-collapse A(h(c)) = log Σ_v e^{⟨h,w_v⟩} (eq. 6); A doesn't depend on y, temperature→0 gives margin max_v⟨h,w_v⟩−⟨h,w_y⟩, and minimizers satisfy ⟨h(c),w_v⟩ = log p(v|c)+b(c), identified only up to GL(k), not O(k) (pp. 6–7; proof p. 23). So NTP's positives are a prefix and its continuation inside one document — shared *wording*, not shared world state.

**Experimental setup (§3, pp. 7–10; App. B, pp. 23–24).** Unified recipe: same LeJEPA objective for every encoder (mean-invariance over two global views + SIGReg, λ=0.02), same projector/optimizer/schedule, on stable-pretraining; no encoder ever sees the other modality. Image encoder ViT-S/16 (2 global 224² + 6 local 96² crops); text encoder BERT (12 layers, width 384, 33M params; BERT-T/B/L of 11M/109M/335M for scaling), trained from scratch in three variants differing only in positives — masked spans (bad views), caption views from different captions of the same image (good views), and causal next-token prediction (pp. 7, 23). Datasets: Flickr30k/Karpathy (29k train images ×5 captions, 1,014 val, 1,000 test) (p. 7); MSR-VTT 7k clips / 1,990 val / 1,000 JSFUSION test with 8 frames (pp. 9, 24); Recap-DataComp texts of 2.16M→940M web images (alt-text + two LLaVA/LLaMA-3-8B recaptions) (p. 10); evaluation on WIT-1024 (PRH protocol, mutual 10-NN and unbiased linear CKA, per-layer max) and COCO 5k Karpathy test (pp. 10, 24, 34). Metrics: mutual 10-NN (fit-free), and R@1/R@5 through one Procrustes rotation fitted on validation pairs (p. 7).

**Main results with numbers.**
- *Good views align*: on Flickr, good-view JEPA / bad-view / next-token reach mutual 10-NN .062/.047/.042, R@1 .044/.027/.021, R@5 .133/.095/.077 (chance .010/.001/.005); NTP trained on caption *pairs* barely moves (.043) (p. 7, Table 1; trajectories p. 8, Fig. 5). With a frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14, good-view R@1 .246 vs bad-view .133, next-token .118 (.137 with pairs), Qwen2.5-0.5B .135; all-mpnet .300 and CLIP text .320 on R@1 but mutual 10-NN .189/.167 vs our .232–.257 (p. 12, Table 2).
- *Nuisance measured*: scene-explained fraction ρ at k=32 is .804 (good) / .655 (bad) / .608 (NTP), with Theorem-3 bounds 12.6/22.1/25.1 and observed errors 33.5/39.4/40.3 — ordering respected (p. 8, Table 6 p. 25). Alignment concentrates in leading spectral directions (correlation .70 on direction 1 decaying to ~.1 by 60) (p. 8, Fig. 6).
- *Ablations*: trimming is the knob that matters (whole captions cost 25%, milder trimming 18%); masking, view count, batch, width, schedule move the mean ≤.016; without gradient clipping 3 of 36 runs collapse (pp. 8–9, Fig. 7, Table 8 p. 27). Text-only STS-B Spearman .612 (good, 2M Recap) vs .501 (bad) vs .377 (NTP) (p. 31).
- *Both sides (MSR-VTT)*: mutual 10-NN .067 (good/good), .059 (bad image/good text), .043, .039; frozen DINOv2 prefers the crop-trained image JEPA (.144 vs .132) (p. 9, Fig. 8, Table 13 p. 31).
- *Scale (WIT-1024, PRH benchmark)*: 33M text JEPA rises .034 (Flickr) → .108 → .111 → .125 on texts of 2.16M/10M/50M images, level with Qwen2.5-3B/7B; same texts, same encoder: bad-view .053 and NTP .071 vs good .108 (p. 10, Fig. 9).
- *Sample efficiency*: good-view reaches .109 at 21.6M samples, which NTP reaches at 900M (.111) — 42× fewer samples, 14× fewer text tokens, 435× fewer unique images; at matched 21.6M samples, .108 vs .071 (p. 11, §4.2, Fig. 1).
- *Beating LLMs*: 109M BERT-B good-view JEPA on texts of 940M images (900M samples, 8–16 GPUs) scores WIT 10-NN .184 vs Qwen2.5-72B .154, Llama-3-70B .151, CLIP text .124, mpnet .118; CKA .507 vs .418; CLIP-H .230 vs .210; COCO .161 vs .108 — i.e. .184 with a model 660× smaller that read 116B tokens vs 15–18T (p. 11, §4.3; p. 12 Table 3; p. 34 Table 16; COCO p. 35 Table 17; lead holds with MAE/I-JEPA/CLIP image encoders, Table 18 p. 35). Caveats: four-seed mean .168, SIGReg-weight sensitivity (.121 for one seed), 43/1,024 WIT captions leak into training texts (pp. 11, 32).
- *Scaling law (§4.4)*: R@1 = a + d log M + b log(1 + q^α M^β N^γ / c) (eq. 7), where q is the fraction of good views, N images, M samples; fits 45 grid cells with RMSE .007 and predicts 85 unseen runs with RMSE .0093, versus .0096 seed-to-seed RMSE (p. 12–13, Fig. 11; detail p. 25). Iso-alignment: q ∝ M^−0.30; unique images enter weakly (γ=.19); the law overestimates good-view runs at 320M samples because it lacks a repeated-data term (p. 13).
- *Applications (§5)*: (1) captioning with only one rotation fitted on pairs — decoder trained on text alone from noisy good-view embeddings, noise matched as σ=(c⁻²−1)^{1/2}≈3; CIDEr .396 Flickr / .668 COCO with frozen DINOv2, rising to .519/.838 (COCO .838, Fig. 10) with Qwen2.5-1.5B decoder + DINOv2-g + DINOv3-L + consensus of 32; rotation beats free linear maps and MLPs out of domain (.832 vs .652/.597 COCO) (p. 13, Tables 9–10 pp. 27, 29). Video: CIDEr .246 on 2,990 MSR-VTT clips, above CLIP-based zero-shot captioners (.058–.186) but below VideoCoCa .271 (p. 13, Table 11 p. 29). (2) **No pairs at all**: with Schnaus et al.'s pair-free method, the 109M JEPA gets FOSCTTM .018 and 86.0% CIFAR-10 top-1, 67.2% CIFAR-100 top-5, 64.4% ImageNet-100 top-5 — above every zero-shot number in that paper (≤82/62/56) and above a rerun Qwen3-8B (.018, 83.4, 61.7, 47.6; p=.003 and p<.001), while NTP fails (FOSCTTM .287) (p. 14, Table 4; details p. 28–30).

**Section map.** §1 Intro & five contributions (pp. 2–3); §2 Theory — 2.1 PRT, 2.2 mismatched positives, 2.3 good/bad-view JEPAs, 2.4 NTP is a bad-view JEPA (pp. 3–7); §3 Empirics on matched encoders — 3.1 cross-modal alignment, 3.2 trimming ablation, 3.3 both sides on video, 3.4 vs a pretrained LM (pp. 7–10); §4 Scaling — 4.1 web text, 4.2 42× sample efficiency, 4.3 beats LLMs to 72B, 4.4 scaling law (pp. 10–13); §5 Applications — 5.1 pair-light captioner, 5.2 pair-free alignment (pp. 13–14); §6 Related work (pp. 14–15); §7 Conclusion + known limitations (population statements, lossy renderings, uniqueness only for second-order anti-collapse, Theorem 2 spectral-only, image side mostly bad-view crops, good views require caption grouping / LLaVA recaptions) (p. 15). Appendix A proofs incl. numerical checks (pp. 20–23); Appendix B experimental details (pp. 23–24); Appendix C extra results — Table 5 text-only, overfitting, nuisance, which-texts ablation, synthetic data, scaling-law detail, recipe robustness, captioner tables/figures, video, pair-free detail, noise, frozen-encoder table, uncertainty intervals, 940M checkpoints, WIT/COCO/vision-family tables, t-SNE and retrieval figures (pp. 24–37).
